title: Rigveda 9.88: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.88: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.88 is a hymn of 8 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 718r-718v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.88.1-3 (aṣṭaka 7, adhyāya 3, varga 24); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 718r
translation.original_text:
1a̱yaṁ soma̍ indra̱ tubhya̍ṁ sunve̱ tubhya̍m pavate̱ tvam a̍sya pāhi | tvaṁ ha̱ yaṁ ca̍kṛ̱ṣe tvaṁ va̍vṛ̱ṣa indu̱m madā̍ya̱ yujyā̍ya̱ soma̍m ||
2sa ī̱ṁ ratho̱ na bhu̍ri̱ṣāḻ a̍yoji ma̱haḥ pu̱rūṇi̍ sā̱taye̱ vasū̍ni | ād ī̱ṁ viśvā̍ nahu̱ṣyā̍ṇi jā̱tā sva̍rṣātā̱ vana̍ ū̱rdhvā na̍vanta ||
3vā̱yur na yo ni̱yutvā̍m̐ i̱ṣṭayā̍mā̱ nāsa̍tyeva̱ hava̱ ā śambha̍viṣṭhaḥ | vi̱śvavā̍ro draviṇo̱dā i̍va̱ tman pū̱ṣeva̍ dhī̱java̍no 'si soma ||
translation.text:
1FOR thee this Soma is effused, O Indra: drink of this juice; for thee the stream is flowing- Soma, which thou thyself hast made and chosen, even Indu, for thy special drink to cheer thee.
2Like a capacious car hath it been harnessed, the Mighty; to acquire abundant treasures. Then in the sacrifice they celebrated all triumphs won by Nahus in the battle.
3Like Vâyu with his team, moving at pleasure, most gracious when invoked like both Nâsatyas, Thou art thyself like the Wealth-Giver, Soma! who grants all boons, like song-inspiring Pûshan.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 718r (numbered 35r by the scribe) (OPenn image 718, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.87.7 ‹satvā›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 718v (numbered 35v by the scribe), begins in RV 9.88.4 ‹na hi tvam ahi-nāmnām›. Verses 9.88.1-3 end on this page.

2saḥ | īm iti | rathaḥ | na | bhuriṣāṭ | ayoji | mahaḥ | purūṇi | sātaye | vasūni | āt | īm iti | viśvā | nahuṣyāṇi | jātā | svaḥ-sātā | vane | ūrdhvā | navanta

translation.original_ref: RV 9.88.4-8 (aṣṭaka 7, adhyāya 3, varga 24); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 718v
translation.original_text:
4indro̱ na yo ma̱hā karmā̍ṇi̱ cakri̍r ha̱ntā vṛ̱trāṇā̍m asi soma pū̱rbhit | pai̱dvo na hi tvam ahi̍nāmnāṁ ha̱ntā viśva̍syāsi soma̱ dasyo̍ḥ ||
5a̱gnir na yo vana̱ ā sṛ̱jyamā̍no̱ vṛthā̱ pājā̍ṁsi kṛṇute na̱dīṣu̍ | jano̱ na yudhvā̍ maha̱ta u̍pa̱bdir iya̍rti̱ soma̱ḥ pava̍māna ū̱rmim ||
6e̱te somā̱ ati̱ vārā̱ṇy avyā̍ di̱vyā na kośā̍so a̱bhrava̍rṣāḥ | vṛthā̍ samu̱draṁ sindha̍vo̱ na nīcī̍ḥ su̱tāso̍ a̱bhi ka̱laśā̍m̐ asṛgran ||
7śu̱ṣmī śardho̱ na māru̍tam pava̱svāna̍bhiśastā di̱vyā yathā̱ viṭ | āpo̱ na ma̱kṣū su̍ma̱tir bha̍vā naḥ sa̱hasrā̍psāḥ pṛtanā̱ṣāṇ na ya̱jñaḥ ||
8rājño̱ nu te̱ varu̍ṇasya vra̱tāni̍ bṛ̱had ga̍bhī̱raṁ tava̍ soma̱ dhāma̍ | śuci̱ṣ ṭvam a̍si pri̱yo na mi̱tro da̱kṣāyyo̍ arya̱mevā̍si soma ||
translation.text:
4Like Indra who hath done great deeds, thou, Soma, art slayer of the Vr̥itras, Fort-destroyer. Like Pedu's horse who killed the brood of serpents, thus thou, O Soma, slayest every Dasyu.
5Like Agni loosed amid the forest, fiercely he winneth splendour in the running waters. Like one who fights, the roaring of the mighty, thus Soma Pavamâna sends his current.
6These Somas passing through the fleecy filter, like rain descending from the clouds of heaven, Have been effused and poured into the beakers, swiftly like rivers running lowly seaward.
7Flow onward like the potent band of Maruts, like that Celestial Host whom none revileth. Quickly be gracious unto us like waters, like sacrifice victorious, thousand-fashioned.
8Thine are King Varuṇa's eternal statutes, lofty and deep, O Soma, is thy glory. All-pure art thou like Mitra the beloved, adorable, like Aryaman, O Soma.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 718v (numbered 35v by the scribe) (OPenn image 719, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.88.4 ‹na hi tvam ahi-nāmnām›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 719r (numbered 36r by the scribe), begins in RV 9.89.2 ‹-śyena-jūtaḥ duhe īm pitā›. Verses 9.88.4-8 end on this page; 9.88.4 begins on fol. 718r (numbered 35r by the scribe).
